evals.prompt: we have billing/invoice_engine.py at like 2,400 lines and nobody on the team dares touch it. every PR that goes near it breaks something in payroll. can you get it into a shape where a new hire could change it safely? tests are thin
evals.expected_output: Work on a refactor branch with characterization tests written first, then small named-refactoring commits, ending with a charter walk and a full report.
expectations: Work happens on a new branch (e.g. refactor/<scope>), never on main
Characterization tests are written and run green before the first refactoring commit
Each commit contains one named refactoring and tests/lint/types are re-run before it
No behavior fixes are mixed in; any bug found is noted for the user instead
The final report lists every file created, changed or deleted with a reason, and flags any file still over 300 lines

evals.prompt: every time we touch lib/sync/worker.ts something unrelated breaks. 1,800 lines, one giant function with a switch on event type repeated in 4 files. help me untangle it without changing what it does
evals.expected_output: Assess with a findings ledger, apply guard clauses and Extract Method, introduce a pattern such as Strategy only for the repeated switch, and justify it in the report.
expectations: A findings ledger is produced with location, smell, charter rule, proposed refactoring and risk per entry
The repeated type switch is replaced via a pattern only because it is duplicated in multiple places, and the report justifies it by the duplication removed
No speculative interface or layer is added that removes no present duplication
The final report records each charter rule as pass, fail or waive with reasons
Final gate run (tests, lint, types) is shown green

evals.prompt: inherited this django monolith from a contractor, views.py does validation, SQL and email sending all in one. restructure into sensible layers, tests green the whole way
evals.expected_output: Clean-tree check and branch, baseline test run, then step-by-step separation of concerns with a green suite after every commit and a final report.
expectations: git status is checked for a clean working tree and a refactor branch is created before edits
A baseline test run is shown green before any refactoring, or the process stops and surfaces a red suite
Files are staged explicitly and build artifacts like __pycache__ are ignored, not added with git add -A
Business logic is separated from I/O (DB, email) in the resulting structure
Before/after gate readings (longest file, longest function, lint count, test count) and the commit list appear in the report
